kural.deTranslation: Sogar mächtige, unterstützte Männer werden zittern, wenn die erzürnten heiligen Seher es wollen
kural.deExplanation: Obwohl sie über zahlreiche Hilfskräfte verfügen, werden diejenigen zugrunde gehen, die dem Zorn des Adligen ausgesetzt sind, dessen Buße grenzenlos ist

kural.deTranslation: Wer sich für Ehefrauen einsetzt, verliert gewaltigen Gewinn. Diese Lust verachten dynamische Männer
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die sich nach ihren Frauen sehnen, werden die Vortrefflichkeit der Tugend nicht erreichen; und genau das ist es, was diejenigen nicht wollen, die darauf bedacht sind, Reichtum zu erwerben

kural.deTranslation: Der seine Frau unmännlich liebt. Sein Reichtum ist für ihn und alles eine Schande
kural.deExplanation: Der Reichtum dessen, der sich (ungeachtet seiner Männlichkeit) der weiblichen Natur seiner Frau hingibt, wird (bei allen Männern) und bei ihm selbst große Schande hervorrufen;

kural.deTranslation: Wer seiner Frau gegenüber unterwürfig ist, fühlt sich immer schüchtern gegenüber den Weisen
kural.deExplanation: Die Gebrechlichkeit, die sich einer Frau hingibt, wird (ihren Ehemann) immer dazu bringen, sich unter den Guten zu schämen

kural.deTranslation: Aus Angst, seine Frau sei rettungslos. Das Vorgehen der Schwächlinge ist unbarmherzig
kural.deExplanation: Das Unterfangen von jemandem, der seine Frau fürchtet und daher keine Glückseligkeit hat, wird niemals Beifall finden

kural.deTranslation: Wer seine Frau fürchtet, hat immer Angst, den Guten und Weisen Gutes zu tun
kural.deExplanation: Wer seine Frau fürchtet, wird immer Angst davor haben, Gutes zu tun (sogar) zum Wohle des Guten

kural.deTranslation: Die Angst vor den Armen ihrer Frauen haben. Schauen Sie kleinlich aus, selbst wenn Sie ein gottähnliches Leben führen
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die die bambusähnlichen Schultern ihrer Frauen fürchten, werden ihrer Männlichkeit beraubt, obwohl sie wie die Götter gedeihen können

kural.deTranslation: Die schüchternen Frauen werden mehr geschätzt als der Mann, der ihrem Willen unterworfen ist
kural.deExplanation: Sogar die Frau, die sich der Scham gegenübersieht, verdient mehr Wertschätzung als die schamlose Männlichkeit, die etwas tut

kural.deTranslation: Von hellhäutigen Ehefrauen, die regiert werden, helfen weder Freunde noch Güte
kural.deExplanation: Wer den Wünschen seiner Frauen nachgibt, wird weder die Bedürfnisse seiner Freunde lindern noch tugendhafte Taten vollbringen

kural.deTranslation: Wer sich den Frauen unterwirft, sieht weder Tugend, Reichtum noch Freude
kural.deExplanation: Von denen, die den Befehlen ihrer Frauen gehorchen, sind weder Taten der Tugend noch des Reichtums noch (sogar) der Freude zu erwarten

kural.deTranslation: Denker mit starkem und weitherzigem Herzen. Vergöttern Sie den schönen Sex nicht durch Torheit
kural.deExplanation: Die Torheit, die aus der Hingabe an eine Frau resultiert, wird niemals bei denen zu finden sein, die einen reflektierenden Geist und einen daraus resultierenden Wohlstand besitzen

kural.deTranslation: Für Gold, nicht für Liebe, beschwört sie ihre Zunge. Männer werden durch geschmückte Schönheiten ruiniert
kural.deExplanation: Die süßen Worte eleganter (Prostituierter) mit Armbändern, die (einen Mann) nicht aus Zuneigung, sondern aus Geiz begehren, werden Kummer hervorrufen

kural.deTranslation: Vermeiden Sie bösartige Huren, die Liebe nur für ihren egoistischen Vorteil vortäuschen
kural.deExplanation: Man muss den Charakter der bösartigen Frauen ermitteln, die, nachdem sie den Reichtum (eines Mannes) festgestellt haben, gutmütig reden (als ob sie es wären) und Geschlechtsverkehr (mit ihnen) vermeiden.

kural.deTranslation: Die falsche Umarmung von Huren ist wie die einer verdammten Leiche im Dunkeln
kural.deExplanation: Die falschen Umarmungen wohlhabender Frauen ähneln (angeheuerten Männern) der Umarmung einer fremden Leiche in einem dunklen Raum

kural.deTranslation: Die Weisen, die den Reichtum der Gnade suchen, erwarten nicht die niedrige Umarmung der Huren
kural.deExplanation: Die Weisen, die nach dem Reichtum der Gnade streben, werden nicht die niedrigen Gunstbeweise derer begehren, die Reichtum (und nicht Vergnügen) als ihren Reichtum betrachten

kural.deTranslation: Die erhabenen Weisen werden niemals die offenen Reize einer abscheulichen Hure begehren
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, deren Wissen durch ihren (natürlichen) Sinn ausgezeichnet ist, werden die unbedeutenden Freuden nicht begehren

kural.deTranslation: Diejenigen, die ihren würdigen Ruhm bewahren, meiden den prahlerischen Charme der Frevler
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die (den Ruhm) ihrer eigenen Güte verbreiten würden, werden nicht die Schultern derer begehren, die sich über ihre Errungenschaften freuen und ihre verabscheuungswürdigen Gunstbeweise (an alle, die dafür zahlen) erweisen.

kural.deTranslation: Hohle Herzen allein begehren die Arme von Huren mit Herzen anderswo
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die keinen vollkommenen (reformierten) Geist haben, werden die Schultern derer begehren, die (sie) umarmen, während ihre Herzen nach anderen Dingen verlangen

kural.deTranslation: Vernunftlose Narren werden durch die Arme von Sirenen angelockt, die in die Irre führen
kural.deExplanation: Die Weisen sagen, dass die Umarmungen treuloser Frauen für diejenigen, denen es an Urteilsvermögen mangelt, genauso verderblich sind wie die Umarmungen der himmlischen Frau

kural.deTranslation: Die weichen, juwelenbesetzten Arme von Huren sind die Hölle, in die die Erniedrigten fallen
kural.deExplanation: Die zarten Schultern von Prostituierten mit hervorragenden Juwelen sind eine Hölle, in die die unwissende Basis gestürzt wird

kural.deTranslation: Doppelzüngige Huren, Wein und Würfel sind Verlockungen derer, denen das Glück im Weg steht
kural.deExplanation: Verräterische Frauen, Alkohol und Glücksspiel sind die Begleiter derjenigen, die das Schicksal verlassen hat

kural.deTranslation: Feinde fürchten sich nicht, wer für Wirbelsturm Die Süchtigen verlieren täglich ihren Ruhm
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die immer nach Alkohol dürsten, werden (bei anderen) weder Angst hervorrufen noch das Licht (ihres Ruhmes) behalten.

kural.deTranslation: Trinken Sie keinen Alkohol; aber lasst sie trinken, wen die Weisen nicht mit Hochachtung denken würden
kural.deExplanation: Es soll kein Alkohol getrunken werden; Wenn es gewünscht wird, soll es von denen getrunken werden, denen die Wertschätzung der Großen egal ist

kural.deTranslation: Die Freude des Trunkenbolds schmerzt selbst das Gesicht der Mutter. Wie abscheulich muss sie für den Weisen aussehen?
kural.deExplanation: Eine Vergiftung ist selbst in Gegenwart der Mutter schmerzhaft; Was wird es dann nicht sein in dem der Weisen?

kural.deTranslation: Die gute Schande wendet sich beschämt von dem ab, der des verurteilten Weines schuldig ist
kural.deExplanation: Die schöne Magd der Bescheidenheit wird denen den Rücken kehren, die sich des großen und abscheulichen Verbrechens der Trunkenheit schuldig gemacht haben

kural.deTranslation: Bezahlen und trinken und den Verstand verlieren ist nichts als grobe Unwissenheit
kural.deExplanation: Geld zu geben und Bewusstlosigkeit zu kaufen, ist das Ergebnis der Unwissenheit über (die eigenen Handlungen)

kural.deTranslation: Sie nehmen Gift, die Toddy nehmen Und dösen sogar wie eine Leiche
kural.deExplanation: Die Schlafenden ähneln der Tat; (ebenso) diejenigen, die trinken, sind keine anderen als Giftfresser

kural.deTranslation: Den heimlichen Trunkenbolden sind die Sinne ausgefallen. Bringen Sie die neugierige Öffentlichkeit zum Lachen
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die sich immer durch ein privates (Genuss-)Getränk berauschen; Ihre Geheimnisse werden entdeckt und von ihren Mitbürgern ausgelacht

kural.deTranslation: Sagen Sie nicht, dass ich kein Trunkenbold bin. Der versteckte Betrug ist im Ausland bekannt
kural.deExplanation: Lass (den Betrunkenen) aufgeben und sagen: „Ich habe noch nie getrunken“; (Denn) In dem Moment, in dem er trinkt, wird er einfach seinen früheren Versuch zu verbergen verraten

kural.deTranslation: Kann man jemanden, der im Wasser versunken ist, mit der Taschenlampe durchsuchen? Kann die Vernunft den tobenden Betrunkenen erreichen?
kural.deExplanation: Mit einem Betrunkenen zu reden ist, als würde man mit einer Taschenlampe unter Wasser gehen, um einen Ertrunkenen zu suchen

kural.deTranslation: Der Nüchterne, der die Notlage des Betrunkenen sieht. Kann er bei sich selbst nicht die gleiche Wirkung spüren?
kural.deExplanation: Wenn (ein Trunkenbold), der nüchtern ist, jemanden sieht, der nicht nüchtern ist, sieht es so aus, als ob er sich nicht an die schädlichen Auswirkungen seines (eigenen) Getränks erinnern würde

kural.deTranslation: Vermeiden Sie Glücksspiele, auch wenn Sie gewinnen. Schluckender Köderhaken – was gewinnt der Fisch?
kural.deExplanation: Auch wenn man gewinnen kann, sollte man doch nicht den Wunsch hegen, zu spielen. (denn) selbst das, was gewonnen wird, ist wie ein Fisch, der das Eisen im Angelhaken verschluckt

kural.deTranslation: Können Spieler im Leben Gutes erreichen, die einhundert verlieren, um zu gewinnen?
kural.deExplanation: Dass sie etwas Gutes erhalten und einen glücklichen Tag erleben? Gibt es tatsächlich einen Lebensunterhalt, der Spielern, die eins gewinnen und hundert verlieren, Glück bescheren kann?

kural.deTranslation: Wenn Könige sich dem Würfeln hingeben, wird ihr ganzes Vermögen den Feinden zufließen
kural.deExplanation: Wenn der König in der Hoffnung auf Gewinn unaufhörlich dem Würfelspiel verfallen ist, werden sein Reichtum und seine Ressourcen verschwinden und in die Hände anderer fallen

kural.deTranslation: Nichts macht dich so arm wie ein Spiel, das nur noch mehr Leid verursacht und deinen Ruhm ruiniert
kural.deExplanation: Nichts bringt (uns) mehr Armut als das Glücksspiel, das viel Leid verursacht und den Ruf zerstört

kural.deTranslation: Das Spiel, die Spielhalle und die Spielerkunst, die mit Freude suchten, sind zunichte geworden
kural.deExplanation: Mittellos sind diejenigen, die aufgrund ihrer Anhaftung niemals das Glücksspiel, den Spielplatz und den Umgang (mit Würfeln) aufgeben würden.

kural.deTranslation: Männer, die von der Ogerin verschluckt wurden, leiden unter Kummer und Not unter diesem Laster
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die von der Göttin namens „Glücksspiel“ verschluckt werden, werden ihren Hunger nie stillen, sondern in der nächsten Welt die Qualen der Hölle erleiden

kural.deTranslation: Wenn Männer ihre Zeit in der Wildhöhle verbringen, enden der Reichtum und die Tugenden ihrer Vorfahren
kural.deExplanation: Zeit am Ort des Glücksspiels zu verschwenden, wird den ererbten Reichtum und die Güte des Charakters zerstören

kural.deTranslation: Spiel ruiniert Reichtum und verdirbt Gnade. Es führt zu Lügen und elendem Leid
kural.deExplanation: Glücksspiel zerstört Eigentum, lehrt Unwahrheit, macht dem Wohlwollen ein Ende und bringt Elend mit sich (hier und im Jenseits)

kural.deTranslation: Kleidung, Reichtum, Essen, Ruhm, Bildung – diese fünf werden in der Hand eines Spielers niemals gedeihen
kural.deExplanation: Die Gewohnheit des Glücksspiels verhindert das Erreichen dieser fünf: Kleidung, Reichtum, Nahrung, Ruhm und Bildung

kural.deTranslation: Die Liebe zum Spiel wächst mit jedem Verlust. So wie die Liebe zum Leben mit Leid wächst
kural.deExplanation: So wie der Spieler (sein Laster) liebt, je mehr er dadurch verliert, so liebt die Seele (den Körper), je mehr sie darunter leidet

kural.deTranslation: Blähungen, Galle und Schleim verursachen drei Krankheiten. Ärzte halten es also für mehr oder weniger
kural.deExplanation: Wenn (Nahrung und Arbeit entweder) übermäßig oder mangelhaft sind, werden die drei von (medizinischen) Autoren aufgezählten Dinge, Blähungen, Galle und Schleim, (eine) Krankheit verursachen

kural.deTranslation: Nach der Verdauung braucht jemand, der seinen Körper ernährt, keine Medikamente mehr
kural.deExplanation: Wer isst, nachdem er sich vergewissert hat, dass das, was er (bereits) gegessen hat, verdaut wurde, braucht keine Medizin

kural.deTranslation: Essen Sie Nahrung nach verdauungsförderndem Maß. Das Leben im Körper dauert mit Freude
kural.deExplanation: Wenn jemand seine Nahrung verdaut hat, soll er in Maßen essen; (denn) das ist der Weg, das Leben einer verkörperten Seele zu verlängern

kural.deTranslation: Kennen Sie die Verdauung; mit gutem Appetit. Iss, was angemessen und richtig ist
kural.deExplanation: (Zuerst) vergewissern Sie sich, dass Ihre Nahrung verdaut wurde, und lassen Sie es nie unterlassen, auch wenn Sie sehr hungrig sind, alles zu essen, was (für Sie) nicht unangenehm ist.

kural.deTranslation: Mit dem richtigen Fasten heilt die richtige Ernährung Lebenskrankheiten und macht strahlend
kural.deExplanation: Es wird keine Katastrophe für das Leben geben, wenn man in Maßen isst, also nicht unangenehme Speisen

kural.deTranslation: Wer mit sauberem Magen isst, wird gesund. Der gierige Vielfraß bleibt krank
kural.deExplanation: Wie Freude bei dem wohnt, der mäßig isst, so wohnt Krankheit bei dem Vielfraß, der gefräßig isst

kural.deTranslation: die jenseits des Feuers des Hungers sättigen und hier unter unzähligen Krankheiten leiden
kural.deExplanation: Wer maßlos isst und die Gesundheitsregeln nicht kennt, wird an unzähligen Krankheiten leiden.

kural.deTranslation: Testen Sie die Krankheit, ihre Ursache und Heilung und wenden Sie ein sicheres Heilmittel an
kural.deExplanation: Lassen Sie den Arzt die (Natur der) Krankheit, ihre Ursache und ihre Heilungsmethode untersuchen und sie gewissenhaft gemäß (medizinischer Regel) behandeln.

kural.deTranslation: Lassen Sie den erfahrenen Arzt die Kranken, die Krankheit, die Jahreszeit und die Behandlung notieren
kural.deExplanation: Der Gelehrte (Arzt) sollte den Zustand seines Patienten feststellen; die Art seiner Krankheit und die Jahreszeit (des Jahres) und (dann) fortfahren (mit seiner Behandlung)

kural.deTranslation: Patient, Arzt, Medizin und Krankenschwester sind vierfache Codes des Behandlungsablaufs
kural.deExplanation: Die medizinische Wissenschaft besteht aus vier Teilen, nämlich dem Patienten, dem Arzt, der Medizin und dem Therapeuten. und jede davon enthält (wieder) vier Unterteilungen

kural.deTranslation: Rechter Menschenverstand und Schüchternheit schmücken von Natur aus nur die Edelgeborenen
kural.deExplanation: Beständigkeit (in Gedanken, Worten und Taten) und Angst (vor der Sünde) sind nur für Hochgeborene gleichermaßen natürlich

kural.deTranslation: Den Adligen fehlen diese drei nicht: Gutes Benehmen, Wahrheit und Bescheidenheit
kural.deExplanation: Der Hochgeborene wird niemals von diesen drei abweichen; gute Manieren, Ehrlichkeit und Bescheidenheit

kural.deTranslation: Lächeln, Geschenk, süße Worte und Höflichkeit Diese vier kennzeichnen wahren Adel
kural.deExplanation: Ein fröhliches Gesicht, Großzügigkeit, angenehme Worte und ein unverschämtes Gemüt – diese vier gelten als die typischen Eigenschaften eines wahrhaft Hochgeborenen

kural.deTranslation: Selbst für crores kann sich die edle Stimmung keiner erniedrigenden Tat beugen
kural.deExplanation: Obwohl er mit immensem Reichtum gesegnet ist, wird der Adlige niemals etwas Unziemliches tun

kural.deTranslation: Die Möglichkeiten der Schenkung können schwinden; Dennoch bewahren alte Häuser ihre edle Eigenschaft
kural.deExplanation: Obwohl ihre Mittel sinken, werden diejenigen, die in alten Familien geboren wurden, ihren Charakter (für Liberalität) nicht verlieren.

kural.deTranslation: Wer das Prestige seiner Familie hütet, beugt sich nicht vor listigen Verlockungen
kural.deExplanation: Wer die tadellose Ehre seiner Familien wahren will, wird nicht bösartig das tun, was ihr abträglich ist

kural.deTranslation: Die Fehler der Adligen sind zu sehen wie am Himmel die Flecken des Mondes
kural.deExplanation: Als Flecken auf ihrer hellen Kugel erhaben sie den Abendhimmel

kural.deTranslation: Wenn die Manieren der Guten unhöflich sind, halten die Menschen ihre Abstammung für unhöflich
kural.deExplanation: Wenn jemand aus einer guten Familie einen Mangel an Zuneigung verrät, wird seine Abstammung von dieser Familie in Frage gestellt

kural.deTranslation: Die Natur des Bodens zeigt sich im Keimen. Der Wert der Geburt strömt aus Worten
kural.deExplanation: So wie der Spross die Beschaffenheit des Bodens anzeigt, so zeigt die Rede des Adligen (die seiner Geburt) an.

kural.deTranslation: Alle erlangen einen guten Namen durch Bescheidenheit, Adel durch Demut
kural.deExplanation: Wer sich einen guten Namen wünscht, muss sich Bescheidenheit wünschen; und wer die Größe einer Familie wünscht, muss allen gegenüber unterwürfig sein

kural.deTranslation: Obwohl es für Ihr Leben im Wesentlichen notwendig ist, unterlassen Sie gemeine, erniedrigende Handlungen
kural.deExplanation: Handlungen, die die Familie schädigen würden, sollten nicht unternommen werden; obwohl sie möglicherweise so wichtig sind, dass ihre Nichtbeachtung mit dem Tod enden würde

kural.deTranslation: Wer nach Ehre und männlichem Ruhm strebt, tut nicht einmal wegen seines Namens gemeine Taten
kural.deExplanation: Wer seine Ehre bewahren möchte, wird sicherlich nichts Unehrenhaftes tun, auch nicht um Ruhm zu erlangen

kural.deTranslation: Seien Sie demütig im Wohlstand, wahren Sie im Niedergang die Würde
kural.deExplanation: In großem Wohlstand ist Demut angebracht; Würde, in großer Not

kural.deTranslation: Wie Haare vom Kopf fallen diejenigen, die von ihrem hohen Status fallen
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die von ihrer (hohen) Position gefallen sind, sind wie die Haare, die vom Kopf gefallen sind

kural.deTranslation: Sogar bergähnliche Männer werden zunichte gemacht, mit abruskornähnlichen kleinen Fehlern
kural.deExplanation: Sogar diejenigen, die wie ein Hügel erhöht sind, werden für niedrig gehalten, wenn sie erniedrigende Taten begehen

kural.deTranslation: Warum schmeicheln Sie Männern, die Sie hier verachten? Es bringt weder Ruhm noch himmlische Glückseligkeit
kural.deExplanation: Warum sollte man Männern folgen, die verachten, und auf ihren Befehl warten?

kural.deTranslation: Besser ist es, verlassen zu sterben, als als Sklave der Verächter zu leben
kural.deExplanation: Für einen Mann ist es besser, von ihm zu sagen, dass er in seinem üblichen Zustand gestorben ist, als dass er sein Leben damit verbracht hat, denen zu folgen, die ihn in Ungnade gefallen haben

kural.deTranslation: Ist das Stillen von Körpernektar süß, auch wenn die Ehre verloren geht?
kural.deExplanation: Wenn die Hochgeborenen ihren Körper am Leben behalten, wenn ihre Ehre verloren ist, wird dies sicherlich kein Heilmittel gegen den Tod sein

kural.deTranslation: Die Ehre ist verloren, der Edle vergeht wie ein Yak, der seine Haare verliert
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, die (ihr) Leben aufgeben, wenn (ihre) Ehre auf dem Spiel steht, sind wie der Idiot, der sich selbst tötet, wenn er (auch nur eines seiner) Haare verliert

kural.deTranslation: Ihr Licht wird von der Welt verehrt und gepriesen. Wer wird nicht leben, wenn die Ehre versagt
kural.deExplanation: Die Welt wird (immer) den Ruhm der Ehrenhaften loben und anbeten, die lieber sterben würden, als Empörung zu erleiden

kural.deTranslation: Ein mutiges Herz lebt im Licht. Ohne das ist das Leben Nacht
kural.deExplanation: Das Licht eines Menschen ist die Fülle seines Mutes; Die eigene Dunkelheit ist der Wunsch, ohne diesen (Geisteszustand) zu leben.

kural.deTranslation: Alle Wesen sind von Geburt an gleich, aber die Arbeit entscheidet über ihren unterschiedlichen Wert
kural.deExplanation: Alle Menschen sind sich hinsichtlich ihrer Geburt einig, unterscheiden sich jedoch hinsichtlich ihrer Eigenschaften aufgrund der unterschiedlichen Qualität ihrer Handlungen

kural.deTranslation: Sie sind unedel hoch, nicht hoch. Sie sind edel niedrig, nicht niedrig
kural.deExplanation: Obwohl (erhöht) die Basis nicht groß werden kann; Auch wenn das Große erniedrigt wird, kann es nicht niedrig werden

kural.deTranslation: Größe wie die Keuschheit einer Frau wird von Selbstuntreue bewacht
kural.deExplanation: Existiert, während für sich selbst wahr ist

kural.deTranslation: Große Seelen vollbringen mächtige Taten, die selten zu erreichen sind, wenn ihr Wille aktiv ist
kural.deExplanation: (Wenn auch reduziert) werden die Großen in der Lage sein, Taten richtig auszuführen, die (für andere) schwierig sind.

kural.deTranslation: Die Kleinmütigen haben nicht den Mut, die Großen zu suchen und sich mit ihnen anzufreunden
kural.deExplanation: Es liegt niemals in der Natur der Basis, die Gesellschaft der Großen zu suchen und an ihrer Natur teilzuhaben

kural.deTranslation: Die Basis mit Kraft und Opulenz Wachs mit Taten der Unverschämtheit
kural.deExplanation: Sogar Adel der Abstammung, Reichtum und Gelehrsamkeit wird, wenn er die Basis besitzt, (nur) immer größeren Stolz hervorrufen

kural.deTranslation: Größe beugt sich mit Bescheidenheit, Gemeinheit prahlt mit Eitelkeit
kural.deExplanation: Der Große wird sich immer demütigen; aber der Mittelmäßige wird sich in Selbstbewunderung erheben

kural.deTranslation: Größe ist frei von Unverschämtheit. Kleinheit schwillt mit dieser Beleidigung an
kural.deExplanation: Freiheit von Selbstgefälligkeit ist (die Natur wahrer) Größe; (während) Hartnäckigkeit darin Gemeinheit ist

kural.deTranslation: Die Schwäche anderer verbirgt die Größe der Kleinen. Allein die Mängel verkünden dies
kural.deExplanation: Die Großen verbergen die Fehler anderer; Die Basis gibt sie nur preis

kural.deTranslation: Alles Gute ist Pflicht gegenüber denen, die pflichtbewusst und erhaben sind
kural.deExplanation: Es heißt, dass diejenigen, die sich ihrer Pflicht bewusst sind und sich mit vollkommener Güte verhalten, alles Gute als natürlich betrachten

kural.deTranslation: Das Gute im Großen ist der Charakter, als dass es nichts Besseres gibt
kural.deExplanation: Die einzige Freude der Vollkommenen ist ihre Güte; alle anderen (sinnlichen) Genüsse gehören nicht zu den (wahren) Genüssen

kural.deTranslation: Liebe, Wahrheit, Respekt, Bescheidenheit, Anmut Diese fünf sind die Ruhestätte der Tugend
kural.deExplanation: Zuneigung, Angst (vor der Sünde), Wohlwollen, Gunst und Wahrhaftigkeit; Dies sind die fünf Säulen, auf denen vollkommene Güte ruht

kural.deTranslation: Nicht zu töten ist reine Buße. Tugend nicht zu verleumden, gewiss
kural.deExplanation: Buße besteht in der Güte, die nicht tötet, und Vollkommenheit in der Güte, die die Fehler anderer nicht anerkennt

kural.deTranslation: Demut ist die Stärke der Tapferkeit. Eine Kraft, die Feinde lange abwehrt
kural.deExplanation: Sich (zu Untergebenen) zu beugen ist die Stärke derer, die es schaffen (ein Unterfangen); und das ist die Waffe, mit der die Großen ihre Feinde abwehren

kural.deTranslation: Sich von der Mitte abstoßen zu lassen, ist der Prüfstein für würdige Männer
kural.deExplanation: Der Prüfstein für Vollkommenheit besteht darin, selbst durch Untergebene eine Niederlage einzustecken

kural.deTranslation: Was ist der Gewinn der Vollkommenheit, wenn sie nicht Freude als Schmerz zurückgibt?
kural.deExplanation: Was nützt vollkommene Güte, wenn sie selbst denen, die sie gequält haben, nichts Gutes tun kann?

kural.deTranslation: Es gibt keine Schande in der Armut. Für einen Starken in guter Qualität
kural.deExplanation: Armut ist keine Schande für jemanden, der über viele gute Eigenschaften verfügt

kural.deTranslation: Äonen mögen sich ändern, aber nicht der Seher, der ein Meer reiner Tugend ist
kural.deExplanation: Diejenigen, von denen man sagt, dass sie das Ufer des Meeres der Vollkommenheit sind, werden sich niemals ändern, auch wenn sich die Zeiten ändern können

kural.deTranslation: Die Welt wird ihr Gewicht nicht mehr ertragen, wenn die Großen aus hoher Tugend fallen
kural.deExplanation: Wenn es einen Mangel im Charakter des Vollkommenen gibt, kann (selbst) die große Welt (ihre) Last nicht tragen

kural.deTranslation: Zur Höflichkeit ohne Zugang kommt leicht Höflichkeit
kural.deExplanation: Wenn man leicht zu allem Zugang hat, wird es für einen leicht sein, die Tugend namens Güte zu erlangen

kural.deTranslation: Menschlichkeit und edle Abstammung Entwickeln Sie Höflichkeit und moralischen Wert
kural.deExplanation: Zuneigung und die Herkunft aus einer guten Familie sind das, was man als angemessenes Verhalten gegenüber allen bezeichnet

kural.deTranslation: Ähnlichkeit in den Gliedmaßen ist keine Ähnlichkeit, sondern Ähnlichkeit in freundlicher Höflichkeit
kural.deExplanation: Ähnlichkeit von Körpern ist keine Ähnlichkeit von Seelen; Wahre Ähnlichkeit ist die Ähnlichkeit von Eigenschaften, die anziehend wirken

kural.deTranslation: Die Welt applaudiert diesen hilfsbereiten Männern, deren Handlungen gerecht und gütig sind
kural.deExplanation: Die Welt lobt den Charakter derjenigen, deren Nützlichkeit sich aus ihrer Gerechtigkeit und Barmherzigkeit ergibt

kural.deTranslation: Die Höflichen verabscheuen nicht einmal ihre Feinde. Denn Verachtung beleidigt sogar im Scherz
kural.deExplanation: Vorwürfe sind für einen selbst im Sport schmerzhaft; Diejenigen, die (deshalb) die Natur anderer kennen, zeigen (erfreuliche) Eigenschaften, selbst wenn sie gehasst werden

kural.deTranslation: Die Welt ruht bei den besten Manieren, sonst zerfällt sie und zerfällt zu Staub
kural.deExplanation: Der (Weg der) Welt besteht durch den Kontakt mit dem Guten; andernfalls würde es sich in der Erde vergraben und zugrunde gehen

kural.deTranslation: Die manierlosen, wenn auch scharfen Feile sind wie unbeugsame Holzklötze
kural.deExplanation: Wer keine (wahren) menschlichen Eigenschaften hat, ähnelt (nur) einem Baum, obwohl er möglicherweise die Schärfe einer Feile besitzt

kural.deTranslation: Unhöflichkeit ist in der Tat gemein, selbst gegenüber einer unfreundlichen Rasse
kural.deExplanation: Es ist falsch (für die Weisen), keine (guten) Eigenschaften zu zeigen, selbst gegenüber denen, die keine Freundschaft (für sie) hegen und nur hasserfüllte Dinge tun

kural.deTranslation: Für diejenigen, denen das lächelnde Licht fehlt. Selbst am Tag ist die Erde Nacht
kural.deExplanation: Für diejenigen, die sich nicht freuen können: Die weite Welt ist selbst im (hellen) Tageslicht begrabene Dunkelheit

kural.deTranslation: Der Reichtum, der durch die mürrische Basis angehäuft wird, ist reine Milch, die durch unreine Vase sauer wird
kural.deExplanation: Der große Reichtum, den jemand erlangt, der nichts Gutes hat, wird vergehen wie reine Milch, die von ihm verdorben wird

kural.deTranslation: Er ist tot und hat Reichtum in Hülle und Fülle. Ohne Genuß, es ist sinnlos
kural.deExplanation: Wer sich nicht an den immensen Reichtümern erfreut, die er in seinem Haus angehäuft hat, ist tot, denn er hat nichts erreicht.

kural.deTranslation: Der geizige Geizhals denkt, dass er nur Reichtum hortet und nicht gibt, er ist der geborene Teufel
kural.deExplanation: Wer weiß, dass Reichtum jedes Vergnügen bringt und dennoch so blind ist, ein geiziges Leben zu führen, wird als Dämon geboren

kural.deTranslation: A burden he is to earth indeed Who hoards without a worthy deed
kural.deExplanation: A burden to the earth are men bent on the acquisition of riches and not (true) fame

kural.deTranslation: What legacy can he leave behind Who is for approach too unkind
kural.deExplanation: What will the miser who is not liked (by any one) regard as his own (in the world to come) ?

kural.deTranslation: Was nützen die Crores, die sie horten, um sie zu geben und zu genießen, deren Herz hart ist?
kural.deExplanation: Those who neither give (to others) nor enjoy (their property) are (truly) destitute, though possessing immense riches

kural.deTranslation: Great wealth unused for oneself nor To worthy men is but a slur
kural.deExplanation: He who enjoys not (his riches) nor relieves the wants of the worthy is a disease to his wealth

kural.deTranslation: Who loaths to help have-nots, his gold Is like a spinster-belle grown old
kural.deExplanation: The wealth of him who never bestows anything on the destitute is like a woman of beauty growing old without a husband

kural.deTranslation: Der müßige Reichtum unersuchter Menschen ist ein Giftfruchtbaum inmitten einer Stadt
kural.deExplanation: The wealth of him who is disliked (by all) is like the fruit-bearing of the etty tree in the midst of a town

kural.deTranslation: Others usurp the shining gold In loveless, stingy, vicious hold
kural.deExplanation: To heap up glittering wealth, their hoards shall others take

kural.deTranslation: The brief want of the rich benign Is like rainclouds growing thin
kural.deExplanation: The short-lived poverty of those who are noble and rich is like the clouds becoming poor (for a while)

kural.deTranslation: To shrink from evil deed is shame The rest is blush of fair-faced dame
kural.deExplanation: True modesty is the fear of (evil) deeds; all other modesty is (simply) the bashfulness of virtuous maids

kural.deTranslation: Food, dress and such are one for all Modesty marks the higher soul
kural.deExplanation: Food, clothing and the like are common to all men but modesty is peculiar to the good

kural.deTranslation: All lives have their lodge in flesh Perfection has its home in blush
kural.deExplanation: As the body is the abode of the spirit, so the excellence of modesty is the abode of perfection

kural.deTranslation: Shame is the jewel of dignity Shameless swagger is vanity
kural.deExplanation: Is not the modesty ornament of the noble ? Without it, their haughtiness would be a pain (to others)

kural.deTranslation: In them resides the sense of shame Who blush for their and other's blame
kural.deExplanation: The world regards as the abode of modesty him who fear his own and other's guilt

kural.deTranslation: The great refuse the wonder-world Without modesty's hedge and shield
kural.deExplanation: The great make modesty their barrier (of defence) and not the wide world

kural.deTranslation: For shame their life the shame-sensed give Loss of shame they won't outlive
kural.deExplanation: The modest would rather lose their life for the sake of modesty than lose modesty for the sake of life

kural.deTranslation: Virtue is much ashamed of him Who shameless does what others shame
kural.deExplanation: Virtue is likely to forsake him who shamelessly does what others are ashamed of

kural.deTranslation: Lapse in manners injures the race Want of shame harms every good grace
kural.deExplanation: Want of manners injures one's family; but want of modesty injures one's character

kural.deTranslation: Movements of the shameless in heart Are string-led puppet show in fact
kural.deExplanation: The actions of those who are without modesty at heart are like those of puppet moved by a string

kural.deTranslation: No greatness is grander like Saying \"I shall work without slack\"
kural.deExplanation: There is no higher greatness than that of one saying I will not cease in my effort (to raise my family)

kural.deTranslation: These two exalt a noble home Ardent effort and ripe wisdom
kural.deExplanation: One's family is raised by untiring perseverance in both effort and wise contrivances

kural.deTranslation: When one resolves to raise his race Loin girt up God leads his ways
kural.deExplanation: The Deity will clothe itself and appear before him who resolves on raising his family

kural.deTranslation: Who raise their races with ceaseless pain No need for plan; their ends will gain
kural.deExplanation: Those who are prompt in their efforts (to better their family) need no deliberation, such efforts will of themselves succeed

kural.deTranslation: Who keeps his house without a blame People around, his kinship claim
kural.deExplanation: People will eagerly seek the friendship of the prosperous soul who has raised his family without foul means

kural.deTranslation: Who raise their race which gave them birth Are deemed as men of manly worth
kural.deExplanation: A man's true manliness consists in making himself the head and benefactor of his family

kural.deTranslation: Like dauntless heroes in battle field The home-burden rests on the bold
kural.deExplanation: Amid his kindred so the burthen rests upon the strong

kural.deTranslation: No season have they who raise their race Sloth and pride will honour efface
kural.deExplanation: As a family suffers by (one's) indolence and false dignity there is to be so season (good or bad) to those who strive to raise their family

kural.deTranslation: Is not his frame a vase for woes Who from mishaps shields his house?
kural.deExplanation: Is it only to suffering that his body is exposed who undertakes to preserve his family from evil ?

kural.deTranslation: A house will fall by a mishap With no good man to prop it up
kural.deExplanation: If there are none to prop up and maintain a family (in distress), it will fall at the stroke of the axe of misfortune

kural.deTranslation: Farming though hard is foremost trade Men ply at will but ploughmen lead
kural.deExplanation: Agriculture, though laborious, is the most excellent (form of labour); for people, though they go about (in search of various employments), have at last to resort to the farmer

kural.deTranslation: Tillers are linch-pin of mankind Bearing the rest who cannot tend
kural.deExplanation: Agriculturists are (as it were) the linch-pin of the world for they support all other workers who cannot till the soil

kural.deTranslation: They live who live to plough and eat The rest behind them bow and eat
kural.deExplanation: They alone live who live by agriculture; all others lead a cringing, dependent life

kural.deTranslation: Who have the shade of cornful crest Under their umbra umbrellas rest
kural.deExplanation: Patriotic farmers desire to bring all other states under the control of their own king

kural.deTranslation: Who till and eat, beg not; nought hide But give to those who are in need
kural.deExplanation: Those whose nature is to live by manual labour will never beg but give something to those who beg

kural.deTranslation: Should ploughmen sit folding their hands Desire-free monks too suffer wants
kural.deExplanation: If the farmer's hands are slackened, even the ascetic state will fail

kural.deTranslation: Moulds dried to quarter-dust ensure Rich crops without handful manure
kural.deExplanation: If the land is dried so as to reduce one ounce of earth to a quarter, it will grow plentifully even without a handful of manure

kural.deTranslation: Better manure than plough; then weed; Than irrigating, better guard
kural.deExplanation: Manuring is better than ploughing; after weeding, watching is better than watering (it)

kural.deTranslation: If landsmen sit sans moving about The field like wife will sulk and pout
kural.deExplanation: If the owner does not (personally) attend to his cultivation, his land will behave like an angry wife and yield him no pleasure

kural.deTranslation: Fair good earth will laugh to see Idlers pleading poverty
kural.deExplanation: The maiden, Earth, will laugh at the sight of those who plead poverty and lead an idle life

kural.deTranslation: What gives more pain than scarcity? No pain pinches like poverty
kural.deExplanation: There is nothing that afflicts (one) like poverty

kural.deTranslation: The sinner Want is enemy dire Of joys of earth and heaven there
kural.deExplanation: When cruel poverty comes on, it deprives one of both the present and future (bliss)

kural.deTranslation: The craving itch of poverty Kills graceful words and ancestry
kural.deExplanation: Hankering poverty destroys at once the greatness of (one's) ancient descent and (the dignity of one's) speech

kural.deTranslation: Want makes even good familymen Utter words that are low and mean
kural.deExplanation: Even in those of high birth, poverty will produce the fault of uttering mean words

kural.deTranslation: The pest of wanton poverty Brings a train of misery
kural.deExplanation: The misery of poverty brings in its train many (more) miseries

kural.deTranslation: The poor men's words are thrown away Though from heart good things they say
kural.deExplanation: The words of the poor are profitless, though they may be sound in thought and clear in expression

kural.deTranslation: Even the mother looks as stranger The poor devoid of character
kural.deExplanation: He that is reduced to absolute poverty will be regarded as a stranger even by his own mother

kural.deTranslation: The killing Want of yesterday Will it pester me even to-day?
kural.deExplanation: Is the poverty that almost killed me yesterday, to meet me today too ?

kural.deTranslation: One may sleep in the midst of fire In want a wink of sleep is rare
kural.deExplanation: One may sleep in the midst of fire; but by no means in the midst of poverty

kural.deTranslation: Renounce their lives the poor must Or salt and gruel go to waste
kural.deExplanation: The destitute poor, who do not renounce their bodies, only consume their neighbour's salt and water

kural.deTranslation: Demand from those who can supply Default is theirs when they deny
kural.deExplanation: If you meet with those that may be begged of, you may beg; (but) if they withhold (their gift) it is their blame and not yours

kural.deTranslation: Even demand becomes a joy When the things comes without annoy
kural.deExplanation: Even begging may be pleasant, if what is begged for is obtained without grief (to him that begs)

kural.deTranslation: Request has charm form open hearts Who know the duty on their part
kural.deExplanation: There is even a beauty in standing before and begging of those who are liberal in their gifts and understand their duty (to beggars)

kural.deTranslation: Like giving even asking seems From those who hide not even in dreams
kural.deExplanation: To beg of such as never think of withholding (their charity) even in their dreams, is in fact the same as giving (it oneself);

kural.deTranslation: The needy demand for help because The world has men who don't refuse
kural.deExplanation: As there are in the world those that give without refusing, there are (also) those that prefer to beg by simply standing before them

kural.deTranslation: The pain of poverty shall die Before the free who don't deny
kural.deExplanation: All the evil of begging will be removed at the sight of those who are far from the evil of refusing

kural.deTranslation: When givers without scorn impart A thrill of delight fills the heart
kural.deExplanation: Beggars rejoice exceedingly when they behold those who bestow (their alms) with kindness and courtesy

kural.deTranslation: This grand cool world shall move to and fro Sans Askers like a puppet show
kural.deExplanation: If there were no beggars, (the actions done in) the cool wide world would only resemble the movement of a puppet

kural.deTranslation: Where stands the glory of givers Without obligation seekers?
kural.deExplanation: What (praise) would there be to givers (of alms) if there were no beggars to ask for and reveive (them)

kural.deTranslation: The needy should not scowl at \"No\" His need another's need must show * Saint valluvar talks of two kinds of Asking:() Asking help for public causes or enterprises () Begging when one is able to work and this is condemned
kural.deExplanation: He who begs ought not to be angry (at a refusal); for even the misery of (his own) poverty should be a sufficient reason (for so doing)

kural.deTranslation: Not to beg is billions worth E'en from eye-like friends who give with mirth
kural.deExplanation: Not to beg (at all) even from those excellent persons who cheerfully give without refusing, will do immense good

kural.deTranslation: Let World-Maker loiter and rot If \"beg and live\" be human fate
kural.deExplanation: If the Creator of the world has decreed even begging as a means of livelihood, may he too go abegging and perish

kural.deTranslation: Nothing is hard like hard saying \"We end poverty by begging\"
kural.deExplanation: There is no greater folly than the boldness with which one seeks to remedy the evils of poverty by begging (rather than by working)

kural.deTranslation: All space is small before the great Who beg not e'en in want acute
kural.deExplanation: Even the whole world cannot sufficiently praise the dignity that would not beg even in the midst of destitution

kural.deTranslation: Though gruel thin, nothing is sweet Like the food earned by labour's sweat
kural.deExplanation: Even thin gruel is ambrosia to him who has obtained it by labour

kural.deTranslation: It may be water for the cow Begging tongue is mean anyhow
kural.deExplanation: There is nothing more disgraceful to one's tongue than to use it in begging water even for a cow

kural.deTranslation: If beg they must I beg beggers Not to beg from shrinking misers
kural.deExplanation: I beseech all beggars and say, "If you need to beg, never beg of those who give unwillingly."

kural.deTranslation: The hapless bark of beggary splits On the rock of refusing hits
kural.deExplanation: The unsafe raft of begging will split when it strikes on the rock of refusal

kural.deTranslation: The heart at thought of beggars melts; It dies at repulsing insults
kural.deExplanation: To think of (the evil of) begging is enough to melt one's heart; but to think of refusal is enough to break it

kural.deTranslation: The word \"No\" kills the begger's life Where can the niggard's life be safe?
kural.deExplanation: Saying "No" to a beggar takes away his life. (but as that very word will kill the refuser) where then would the latter's life hide itself ?

kural.deTranslation: The mean seem men only in form We have never seen such a sham
kural.deExplanation: The base resemble men perfectly (as regards form); and we have not seen such (exact) resemblance (among any other species)

kural.deTranslation: The base seem richer than the good For no care enters their heart or head
kural.deExplanation: The low enjoy more felicity than those who know what is good; for the former are not troubled with anxiety (as to the good)

kural.deTranslation: The base are like gods; for they too As prompted by their desire do
kural.deExplanation: The base resemble the Gods; for the base act as they like

kural.deTranslation: When the base meets a rake so vile Him he will exceed, exult and smile
kural.deExplanation: The base feels proud when he sees persons whose acts meaner than his own

kural.deTranslation: Fear forms the conduct of the low Craving avails a bit below
kural.deExplanation: (The principle of) behaviour in the mean is chiefly fear; if not, hope of gain, to some extent

kural.deTranslation: The base are like the beaten drum Since other's secrets they proclaim
kural.deExplanation: The base are like a drum that is beaten, for they unburden to others the secrets they have heard

kural.deTranslation: The base their damp hand will not shake But for fists clenched their jaws to break
kural.deExplanation: The mean will not (even) shake off (what sticks to) their hands (soon after a meal) to any but those who would break their jaws with their clenched fists

kural.deTranslation: The good by soft words profits yield The cane-like base when crushed and killed
kural.deExplanation: The great bestow (their alms) as soon as they are informed; (but) the mean, like the sugar-cane, only when they are tortured to death

kural.deTranslation: Faults in others the mean will guess On seeing how they eat and dress
kural.deExplanation: The base will bring an evil (accusation) against others, as soon as he sees them (enjoying) good food

kural.deTranslation: The base hasten to sell themselves From doom to flit and nothing else
kural.deExplanation: The base will hasten to sell themselves as soon as a calamity has befallen them. For what else are they fitted ?

kural.deTranslation: Is it an angel? A fair peacock Or jewelled belle? To my mind a shock!
kural.deExplanation: Is this jewelled female a celestial, a choice peahen, or a human being ? My mind is perplexed

kural.deTranslation: The counter glances of this belle Are armied dart of the Love-Angel
kural.deExplanation: This female beauty returning my looks is like a celestial maiden coming with an army to contend against me

kural.deTranslation: Not known before -I spy Demise In woman's guise with battling eyes
kural.deExplanation: I never knew before what is called Yama; I see it now; it is the eyes that carry on a great fight with (the help of) female qualities

kural.deTranslation: This artless dame has darting eyes That drink the life of men who gaze
kural.deExplanation: These eyes that seem to kill those who look at them are as it were in hostilities with this feminine simplicity

kural.deTranslation: Is it death, eye or doe? All three In winsome woman's look I see
kural.deExplanation: Is it Yama, (a pair of) eyes or a hind ?- Are not all these three in the looks of this maid ?

kural.deTranslation: If cruel brows unbent, would screen Her eyes won't cause me trembling pain
kural.deExplanation: Her eyes will cause (me) no trembling sorrow, if they are properly hidden by her cruel arched eyebrows

kural.deTranslation: Vest on the buxom breast of her Looks like rutting tusker's eye-cover
kural.deExplanation: The cloth that covers the firm bosom of this maiden is (like) that which covers the eyes of a rutting elephant

kural.deTranslation: Ah these fair brows shatter my might Feared by foemen yet to meet
kural.deExplanation: On her bright brow alone is destroyed even that power of mine that used to terrify the most fearless

kural.deTranslation: Which jewel can add to her beauty With fawn-like looks and modesty?
kural.deExplanation: Of what use are other jewels to her who is adorned with modesty, and the meek looks of a hind ?

kural.deTranslation: To the drunk alone is wine delight Nothing delights like love at sight
kural.deExplanation: Unlike boiled honey which yields delight only when it is drunk, love gives pleasure even when looked at

kural.deTranslation: Her painted eyes, two glances dart One hurts; the other heals my heart
kural.deExplanation: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain, and the other is the cure thereof

kural.deTranslation: Her furtive lightning glance is more Than enjoyment of sexual lore
kural.deExplanation: A single stolen glance of her eyes is more than half the pleasure (of sexual embrace)

kural.deTranslation: She looked; looking bowed her head And love-plant was with water fed
kural.deExplanation: She has looked (at men) and stooped (her head); and that (sign) waters as it were (the corn of) our love

kural.deTranslation: I look; she droops to earth awhile I turn; she looks with gentle smile
kural.deExplanation: When I look, she looks down; when I do not, she looks and smiles gently

kural.deTranslation: No direct gaze; a side-long glance She darts at me and smiles askance
kural.deExplanation: She not only avoids a direct look at me, but looks as it were with a half-closed eye and smiles

kural.deTranslation: Their words at first seem an offence But quick we feel them friendly ones
kural.deExplanation: Though they may speak harshly as if they were strangers, the words of the friendly are soon understood

kural.deTranslation: Harsh little words; offended looks, Are feigned consenting love-lorn tricks
kural.deExplanation: Little words that are harsh and looks that are hateful are (but) the expressions of lovers who wish to act like strangers

kural.deTranslation: What a grace the slim maid has! As I look she slightly smiles
kural.deExplanation: When I look, the pitying maid looks in return and smiles gently; and that is a comforting sign for me

kural.deTranslation: Between lovers we do discern A stranger's look of unconcern
kural.deExplanation: Both the lovers are capable of looking at each other in an ordinary way, as if they were perfect strangers

kural.deTranslation: The words of mouth are of no use When eye to eye agrees the gaze
kural.deExplanation: The words of the mouths are of no use whatever, when there is perfect agreement between the eyes (of lovers)

kural.deTranslation: In this bangled beauty dwell The joys of sight sound touch taste smell
kural.deExplanation: The (simultaneous) enjoyment of the five senses of sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch can only be found with bright braceleted (women)

kural.deTranslation: The cure for ailment is somewhere For fair maid's ill she is the cure
kural.deExplanation: The remedy for a disease is always something different (from it); but for the disease caused by this jewelled maid, she is herself the cure

kural.deTranslation: Is lotus-eyed lord's heaven so sweet As sleep in lover's arms so soft?
kural.deExplanation: Can the lotus-eyed Vishnu's heaven be indeed as sweet to those who delight to sleep in the delicate arms of their beloved ?

kural.deTranslation: Away it burns and cools anear Wherefrom did she get this fire?
kural.deExplanation: From whence has she got this fire that burns when I withdraw and cools when I approach ?

kural.deTranslation: The arms of my flower-tressed maid Whatever I wish that that accord
kural.deExplanation: Each varied form of joy the soul can wish is found

kural.deTranslation: My simple maid has nectar arms Each embrace brings life-thrilling charms
kural.deExplanation: The shoulders of this fair one are made of ambrosia, for they revive me with pleasure every time I embrace them

kural.deTranslation: Ah the embrace of this fair dame Is like sharing one's food at home
kural.deExplanation: The embraces of a gold-complexioned beautiful female are as pleasant as to dwell in one's own house and live by one's own (earnings) after distributing (a portion of it in charity)

kural.deTranslation: Joy is the fast embrace that doth Not admit e'en air between both
kural.deExplanation: To ardent lovers sweet is the embrace that cannot be penetrated even by a breath of breeze

kural.deTranslation: Sulking, feeling and clasping fast These three are sweets of lover's tryst
kural.deExplanation: Love quarrel, reconciliation and intercourse - these are the advantages reaped by those who marry for lust

kural.deTranslation: As knowledge reveals past ignorance So is the belle as love gets close
kural.deExplanation: As (one's) ignorance is discovered the more one learns, so does repeated intercourse with a welladorned female (only create a desire for more)

kural.deTranslation: Soft blessed anicha flower, hail On whom I dote is softer still
kural.deExplanation: May you flourish, O Anicham! you have a delicate nature But my beloved is more delicate than you

kural.deTranslation: You can't liken flowers by many eyed, To her bright eyes, O mind dismayed
kural.deExplanation: O my soul, fancying that flowers which are seen by many can resemble her eyes, you become confused at the sight of them

kural.deTranslation: The bamboo-shouldered has pearl-like smiles Fragrant breath and lance-like eyes
kural.deExplanation: The complexion of this bamboo-shouldered one is that of a shoot; her teeth, are pearls; her breath,

kural.deTranslation: Lily droops down to ground and says I can't equal the jewelled-one's eyes
kural.deExplanation: If the blue lotus could see, it would stoop and look at the ground saying, "I can never resemble the eyes of this excellent jewelled one."

kural.deTranslation: Anicha flower with stem she wears To her breaking waist sad-drum-blares!
kural.deExplanation: No merry drums will be beaten for the (tender) waist of her who has adorned herself with the anicham without having removed its stem

kural.deTranslation: Stars are confused to know which is The moon and which is woman's face
kural.deExplanation: The stars have become confused in their places not being able to distinguish between the moon and the maid's countenance

kural.deTranslation: Are there spots on the lady's face Just as in moon that changes phase?
kural.deExplanation: Could there be spots in the face of this maid like those in the bright full moon ?

kural.deTranslation: Like my lady's face if you shine All my love to you; hail O moon!
kural.deExplanation: If you can indeed shine like the face of women, flourish, O moon, for then would you be worth loving ?

kural.deTranslation: Like the face of my flower-eyed one If you look, then shine alone O moon!
kural.deExplanation: O moon, if you wish to resemble the face of her whose eyes are like (these) flowers, do not appear so as to be seen by all

kural.deTranslation: The soft flower and the swan's down are Like nettles to the feet of the fair
kural.deExplanation: The anicham and the feathers of the swan are to the feet of females, like the fruit of the (thorny) Nerunji

kural.deTranslation: Like milk and honey the dew is sweet From her white teeth whose word is soft
kural.deExplanation: The water which oozes from the white teeth of this soft speeched damsel is like a mixture of milk and honey

kural.deTranslation: Love between me and this lady Is like bond between soul and body
kural.deExplanation: The love between me and this damsel is like the union of body and soul

kural.deTranslation: Depart image in my pupil Giving room to my fair-browed belle!
kural.deExplanation: O you image in the pupil (of my eye)! depart; there is no room for (my) fair-browed beloved

kural.deTranslation: Life with my jewel is existence Death it is her severance
kural.deExplanation: My fair-jewelled one resembles the living soul (when she is in union with me), the dying soul when she leaves me

kural.deTranslation: Can I forget? I recall always The charms of her bright battling eyes
kural.deExplanation: If I had forgotten her who has bright battling eyes, I would have remembered (thee); but I never forget her (Thus says he to her maid)

kural.deTranslation: So subtle is my lover's form Ever in my eyes winking, no harm
kural.deExplanation: My lover would not depart from mine eyes; even if I wink, he would not suffer (from pain); he is so ethereal

kural.deTranslation: My lover in my eyes abides I paint them not lest he hides
kural.deExplanation: As my lover abides in my eyes, I will not even paint them, for he would (then) have to conceal himself

kural.deTranslation: My lover abides in my heart I fear hot food lest he feels hot
kural.deExplanation: As my lover is in my heart, I am afraid of eating (anything) hot, for I know it would pain him

kural.deTranslation: My eyes wink not lest he should hide And him as cruel the townsmen chide
kural.deExplanation: I will not wink, knowing that if I did, my lover would hide himself; and for this reason, this town says, he is unloving

kural.deTranslation: He abides happy in my heart But people mistake he is apart
kural.deExplanation: My lover dwells in my heart with perpetual delight; but the town says he is unloving and (therefore) dwells afar

kural.deTranslation: Pangs of passion find no recourse Except riding *`palmyra horse' * Palmyra horse or 'Madal' is a torture expressive of the burning passion of the lover to the beloved The lover's body is laid on a rough pricking palmyra bed and he is carried along the street with songs of love pangs The parents of the lovers first reproach them and then consent to their marriage
kural.deExplanation: To those who after enjoyment of sexual pleasure suffer (for want of more), there is no help so efficient as the palmyra horse

kural.deTranslation: Pining body and mind lose shame And take to riding of the palm
kural.deExplanation: Having got rid of shame, the suffering body and soul save themselves on the palmyra horse

kural.deTranslation: Once I was modest and manly My love has now Madal only
kural.deExplanation: Modesty and manliness were once my own; now, my own is the palmyra horse that is ridden by the lustful

kural.deTranslation: Rushing flood of love sweeps away The raft of shame and firmness, aye!
kural.deExplanation: The raft of modesty and manliness, is, alas, carried-off by the strong current of lust

kural.deTranslation: Palm-ride and pangs of eventide Are gifts of wreath-like bracelet maid
kural.deExplanation: She with the small garland-like bracelets has given me the palmyra horse and the sorrow that is endured at night

kural.deTranslation: Madal I ride at midnight for My eyes sleep not seeing this fair
kural.deExplanation: Mine eyes will not close in sleep on your mistress's account; even at midnight will I think of mounting the palmyra horse

kural.deTranslation: Her sea-like lust seeks not Madal! Serene is woman's self control
kural.deExplanation: There is nothing so noble as the womanly nature that would not ride the palmyra horse, though plunged a sea of lust

kural.deTranslation: Lust betrays itself in haste Though women are highly soft and chaste
kural.deExplanation: Even the Lust (of women) transgresses its secrecy and appears in public, forgetting that they are too chaste and liberal (to be overcome by it)

kural.deTranslation: My perplexed love roves public street Believing that none knows its secret
kural.deExplanation: And thus, in public ways, perturbed will rove

kural.deTranslation: Fools laugh at me before my eyes For they feel not my pangs and sighs
kural.deExplanation: Even strangers laugh (at us) so as to be seen by us, for they have not suffered

kural.deTranslation: Rumour sustains my existence Good luck! many know not its sense
kural.deExplanation: My precious life is saved by the raise of rumour, and this, to my good luck no others are aware of

kural.deTranslation: Rumour gives me the flower-like belle People know not what rare angel
kural.deExplanation: Not knowing the value of her whose eyes are like flowers this town has got up a rumour about me

kural.deTranslation: I profit by this public rumour Having not, I feel, I have her
kural.deExplanation: Will I not get a rumour that is known to the (whole) town ? For what I have not got is as if I had got it (already)

kural.deTranslation: Rumour inflames the love I seek Or else it becomes bleak and weak
kural.deExplanation: Rumour increases the violence of my passion; without it it would grow weak and waste away

kural.deTranslation: Drink delights as liquor flows Love delights as rumour grows
kural.deExplanation: As drinking liquor is delightful (to one) whenever one is in mirth, so is lust delightful to me whenever it is the subject of rumour

kural.deTranslation: One lasting day we met alone Lasting rumours eclipse our moon
kural.deExplanation: It was but a single day that I looked on (my lover); but the rumour thereof has spread like the seizure of the moon by the serpent

kural.deTranslation: Scandal manures; mother's refrain Waters the growth of this love-pain
kural.deExplanation: This malady (of lust) is manured by the talk of women and watered by the (harsh) words of my mother

kural.deTranslation: To quench the lust by rumour free Is to quench fire by pouring ghee
kural.deExplanation: To say that one could extinguish passion by rumour is like extinguishing fire with ghee

kural.deTranslation: Who said \"fear not\" flared up rumour Why then should I blush this clamour?
kural.deExplanation: When the departure of him who said "fear not" has put me to shame before others, why need I be ashamed of scandal

kural.deTranslation: Town raising this cry, I desire Consent is easy from my sire
kural.deExplanation: The rumour I desire is raised by the town (itself); and my lover would if desired consent (to my following him)

kural.deTranslation: Tell me if you but do not leave, Your quick return to those who live
kural.deExplanation: If it is not departure, tell me; but if it is your speedy return, tell it to those who would be alive then

kural.deTranslation: His sight itself was pleasing, near Embrace pains now by partings fear
kural.deExplanation: His very look was once pleasing; but (now) even intercourse is painful through fear of separation

kural.deTranslation: On whom shall I lay my trust hence While parting lurks in knowing ones?
kural.deExplanation: As even the lover who understands (everything) may at times depart, confidence is hardly possible

kural.deTranslation: He parts whose love told me -fear not Is my trust in him at default?
kural.deExplanation: If he who bestowed his love and said "fear not" should depart, will it be the fault of those who believed in (his) assuring words ?

kural.deTranslation: Stop his parting -my life to save Meeting is rare if he would leave
kural.deExplanation: If you would save (my life), delay the departure of my destined (husband); for if he departs, intercourse will become impossible

kural.deTranslation: His hardness says, \"I leave you now\" Is there hope of his renewed love?
kural.deExplanation: Is hard, when he could stand, and of departure speak to me

kural.deTranslation: Will not my gliding bangles' cry The parting of my lord betray?
kural.deExplanation: Do not the rings that begin to slide down my fingers forebode the separation of my lord ?

kural.deTranslation: Bitter is life in friendless place; Worse is parting love's embrace!
kural.deExplanation: Painful is it to live in a friendless town; but far more painful is it to part from one's lover

kural.deTranslation: Can fire that burns by touch burn like Parting of the hearts love-sick?
kural.deExplanation: Fire burns when touched; but, like the sickness of love, can it also burn when removed ?

kural.deTranslation: Many survive pangs of parting Not I this sore so distressing
kural.deExplanation: As if there were many indeed that can consent to the impossible, kill their pain, endure separation and yet continue to live afterwards

kural.deTranslation: It swells out like baled out spring How to bear this pain so writhing?
kural.deExplanation: I would hide this pain from others; but it (only) swells like a spring to those who drain it

kural.deTranslation: I can't conceal this nor complain For shame to him who caused this pain
kural.deExplanation: I cannot conceal this pain, nor can I relate it without shame to him who has caused it

kural.deTranslation: In life -poles of this wearied frame Are poised the weights of lust and shame
kural.deExplanation: (Both) lust and shame, with my soul for their shoulder pole balance themselves on a body that cannot bear them

kural.deTranslation: My lust is a sea; I do not see A raft to go across safely
kural.deExplanation: There is indeed a flood of lust; but there is no raft of safety to cross it with

kural.deTranslation: What wilt they prove when they are foes Who in friendship bring me woes!
kural.deExplanation: What will they prove when angry tempests lower?

kural.deTranslation: The pleasure in love is oceanful But its pangs are more painful
kural.deExplanation: The pleasure of lust is (as great as) the sea; but the pain of lust is far greater

kural.deTranslation: Wild waves of love I swim shoreless Pining alone in midnight hush
kural.deExplanation: I have swam across the terrible flood of lust, but have not seen its shore; even at midnight I am alone; still I live

kural.deTranslation: Night's mercy lulls all souls to sleep Keeping but me for companionship
kural.deExplanation: The night which graciously lulls to sleep all living creatures, has me alone for her companion

kural.deTranslation: Crueller than that cruel he Are midnight hours gliding slowly
kural.deExplanation: The long nights of these days are far more cruel than the heartless one who is torturing me

kural.deTranslation: Like heart, if my sight reaches him It won't in floods of tears swim!
kural.deExplanation: Could mine eyes travel like my thoughts to the abode (of my absent lord), they would not swim in this flood of tears

kural.deTranslation: The eye pointed him to me; why then They weep with malady and pine?
kural.deExplanation: As this incurable malady has been caused by my eyes which showed (him) to me, why should they now weep for (him)

kural.deTranslation: Why should these dyed eyes grieve now sans Regrets for their thoughtless glance?
kural.deExplanation: The dyed eyes that (then) looked without foresight, why should they now endure sorrow, without feeling sharply (their own fault)

kural.deTranslation: Eyes darted eager glance that day It's funny that they weep today
kural.deExplanation: They themselves looked eagerly (on him) and now they weep. Is not this to be laughed at ?

kural.deTranslation: These eyes left me to endless grief Crying adry without relief
kural.deExplanation: These painted eyes have caused me a lasting mortal disease; and now they can weep no more, the tears having dried up

kural.deTranslation: My eyes causing lust more than sea Suffer that torture sleeplessly
kural.deExplanation: Mine eyes have caused me a lust that is greater than the sea and (they themselves) endure the torture of sleeplessness

kural.deTranslation: Lo! eyes that wrought this love-sickness Are victims of the same themselves
kural.deExplanation: The eyes that have given me this disease have themselves been seized with this (suffering) Oh! I am much delighted

kural.deTranslation: Let tears dry up pining pining In eyes that eyed him longing longing
kural.deExplanation: The eyes that became tender and gazed intently on him, may they suffer so much as to dry up the fountain of their tears

kural.deTranslation: Ther's he whose lips loved, not his heart Yet my eyes pine seeing him not
kural.deExplanation: He is indeed here who loved me with his lips but not with his heart but mine eyes suffer from not seeing him

kural.deTranslation: He comes; no sleep; he goes; no sleep This is the fate of eyes that weep
kural.deExplanation: When he is away they do not sleep; when he is present they do not sleep; in either case, mine eyes endure unbearable agony

kural.deTranslation: Like drum beats eyes declare my heart; From people who could hide his secret?
kural.deExplanation: It is not difficult for the people of this place to understand the secret of those whose eyes, like mine, are as it were beaten drums

kural.deTranslation: My lover's parting, I allowed Whom to complain my hue pallid?
kural.deExplanation: I who (then) consented to the absence of my loving lord, to whom can I (now) relate the fact of my having turned sallow

kural.deTranslation: Claiming it is begot through him Pallor creeps and rides over my frame
kural.deExplanation: Sallowness, as if proud of having been caused by him, would now ride on my person

kural.deTranslation: He seized my beauty and modesty Leaving pangs and Pallor to me
kural.deExplanation: He has taken (away) my beauty and modesty, and given me instead disease and sallowness

kural.deTranslation: He is my thought, his praise my theme Yet this pallor steals over my frame
kural.deExplanation: I think (of him); and what I speak about is but his excellence; still is there sallowness; and this is deceitful

kural.deTranslation: My lover departed me there And pallor usurped my body here
kural.deExplanation: Just as my lover departed then, did not sallowness spread here on my person ?

kural.deTranslation: Just as darkness waits for light-off Pallor looks for lover's arms-off
kural.deExplanation: Just as darkness waits for the failing light; so does sallowness wait for the laxity of my husband's intercourse

kural.deTranslation: From his embrace I turned a nonce This pallor swallowed me at once
kural.deExplanation: I who was in close embrace just turned aside and the moment I did so, sallowness came on me like something to be seized on

kural.deTranslation: On my pallor they cast a slur But none says \"lo he parted her\"
kural.deExplanation: Besides those who say "she has turned sallow" there are none who say "he has forsaken her"

kural.deTranslation: Let all my body become pale If he who took my leave fares well
kural.deExplanation: If he is clear of guilt who has conciliated me (to his departure) let my body suffer its due and turn sallow

kural.deTranslation: Let people call me all pallid But my lover let them not deride
kural.deExplanation: It would be good to be said of me that I have turned sallow, if friends do not reproach with unkindness him who pleased me (then)

kural.deTranslation: Stoneless fruit of love they have Who are beloved by those they love
kural.deExplanation: The women who are beloved by those whom they love, have they have not got the stone-less fruit of sexual delight ?

kural.deTranslation: The lover-and-beloved's self-givings Are like rains to living beings
kural.deExplanation: The bestowal of love by the beloved on those who love them is like the rain raining (at the proper season) on those who live by it

kural.deTranslation: The pride of living is for those Whose love is returned by love so close
kural.deExplanation: The pride that says "we shall live" suits only those who are loved by their beloved (husbands)

kural.deTranslation: Whose love is void of love in turn Are luckless with all esteems they earn
kural.deExplanation: Even those who are esteemed (by other women) are devoid of excellence, if they are not loved by their beloved

kural.deTranslation: What can our lover do us now If he does not requite our love?
kural.deExplanation: He who is beloved by me, what will he do to me, if I am not beloved by him ?

kural.deTranslation: One sided pains; love in both souls Poises well like shoulder poles
kural.deExplanation: Lust, like the weight of the KAVADI, pains if it lies in one end only but pleases if it is in both

kural.deTranslation: This cupid aims at me alone; Knows he not my pallor and pain?
kural.deExplanation: Would not cupid who abides and contends in one party (only) witness the pain and sorrow (in that party)?

kural.deTranslation: None is so firm as she who loves Without kind words from whom she dotes
kural.deExplanation: There is no one in the world so hard-hearted as those who can live without receiving (even) a kind word from their beloved

kural.deTranslation: The lover accords not my desires And yet his words sweeten my ears
kural.deExplanation: Though my beloved bestows no love on one, still are his words sweet to my ears

kural.deTranslation: You tell your grief to listless he Bless my heart! rather fill up sea!
kural.deExplanation: Live, O my soul, would you who relate your great sorrow to strangers, try rather to fill up your own sea (of sorrow)

kural.deTranslation: Love is sweeter than wine; for vast Is its delight at very thought
kural.deExplanation: Sexuality is sweeter than liquor, because when remembered, it creates a most rapturous delight

kural.deTranslation: Pains are off at the lover's thought In all aspects this love is sweet
kural.deExplanation: Even to think of one's beloved gives one no pain Sexuality, in any degree, is always delightful

kural.deTranslation: To sneeze I tried hence but could not Me he tried to think but did not
kural.deExplanation: I feel as if I am going to sneeze but do not, and (therefore) my beloved is about to think (of me) but does not

kural.deTranslation: Have I a place within his heart? Ah from mine he will never depart
kural.deExplanation: He continues to abide in my soul, do I likewise abide in his ?

kural.deTranslation: Shame! My heart often he enters Banning me entry into his
kural.deExplanation: He who has imprisoned me in his soul, is he ashamed to enter incessantly into mine

kural.deTranslation: Beyond the thought of life with him What else of life can I presume?
kural.deExplanation: I live by remembering my (former) intercourse with him; if it were not so, how could I live ?

kural.deTranslation: What will happen if I forget When his memory burns my heart?
kural.deExplanation: I have never forgotten (the pleasure); even to think of it burns my soul; could I live, if I should ever forget it ?

kural.deTranslation: I bring him to ceaseless memory He chides not; and thus honours me
kural.deExplanation: He will not be angry however much I may think of him; is it not so much the delight my beloved

kural.deTranslation: Dear life ebbs away by thought Of him who said we are one heart
kural.deExplanation: My precious life is wasting away by thinking too much on the cruelty of him who said we were not different

kural.deTranslation: Hail moon! Set not so that I find Him who left me but not my mind
kural.deExplanation: May you live, O Moon! Do not set, that I mine see him who has departed without quitting my soul

kural.deTranslation: How shall I feast this dream-vision That brings the beloved's love-mission?
kural.deExplanation: Where with shall I feast the dream which has brought me my dear one's messenger ?

kural.deTranslation: I beg these fish-like dark eyes sleep To tell my lover how life I keep
kural.deExplanation: If my fish-like painted eyes should, at my begging, close in sleep, I could fully relate my sufferings to my lord

kural.deTranslation: In wakeful hours who sees me not I meet in dreams and linger yet
kural.deExplanation: My life lasts because in my dream I behold him who does not favour me in my waking hours

kural.deTranslation: In dreams I enjoy his love-bliss Who in wakeful hours I miss
kural.deExplanation: There is pleasure in my dream, because in it I seek and obtain him who does not visit me in my wakefulness

kural.deTranslation: Dream-sight of him delights at once Awake-What of seeing him -hence
kural.deExplanation: I saw him in my waking hours, and then it was pleasant; I see him just now in my dream, and it is (equally) pleasant

kural.deTranslation: If wakeful hours come to nought My lov'r in dreams would nev'r depart
kural.deExplanation: Were there no such thing as wakefulness, my beloved (who visited me) in my dream would not depart from me

kural.deTranslation: Awake he throws my overtures Adream, ah cruel! he tortures!
kural.deExplanation: The cruel one who would not favour me in my wakefulness, what right has he to torture me in my dreams?

kural.deTranslation: Asleep he embraces me fast; Awake he enters quick my heart
kural.deExplanation: When I am asleep he rests on my shoulders, (but) when I awake he hastens into my soul

kural.deTranslation: In dreams who don't discern lovers Rue their missing in wakeful hours
kural.deExplanation: They who have no dear ones to behold in their dreams blame him who visits me not in my waking hours

kural.deTranslation: The townsmen say he left me thus  In dreams failing to see him close
kural.deExplanation: The women of this place say he has forsaken me in my wakefulness I think they have not seen him visit me in my dreams

kural.deTranslation: Bless you! you are not eventide But killing dart to wedded bride!
kural.deExplanation: Live, O you evening are you (the former) evening? No, you are the season that slays (married) women

kural.deTranslation: Hail sad eventide dim and grim Has your mate like mine, cruel whim!
kural.deExplanation: A long life to you, O dark evening! You are sightless Is your help-mate (also) as hard-hearted as mine

kural.deTranslation: Wet eve came pale and trembling then Now it makes bold with growing pain
kural.deExplanation: The evening that (once) came in with trembling and dimness (now) brings me an aversion for life and increasing sorrow

kural.deTranslation: Lover away, comes eventide Like slayer to field of homicide
kural.deExplanation: In the absence of my lover, evening comes in like slayers on the field of slaughter

kural.deTranslation: What good have I done to morning And what evil to this evening?
kural.deExplanation: O eve, why art thou foe! thou dost renew my grief

kural.deTranslation: Evening pangs I have not known When my lord nev'r left me alone
kural.deExplanation: Previous to my husband's departure, I know not the painful nature of evening

kural.deTranslation: Budding at dawn burgeoning all day This disease blooms in evening gay
kural.deExplanation: This malady buds forth in the morning, expands all day long and blossoms in the evening

kural.deTranslation: A deadly arm, this shepherd's flute Hails flaming eve and slays my heart
kural.deExplanation: The shepherd's flute now sounds as a fiery forerunner of night, and is become a weapon that slays (me)

kural.deTranslation: Deluding eve if it prolongs The whole town will suffer love-pangs
kural.deExplanation: When night comes on confusing (everyone's) mind, the (whole) town will lose its sense and be plunged in sorrow

kural.deTranslation: Thinking of him whose quest is wealth My life outlives the twilight stealth
kural.deExplanation: My (hitherto) unextinguished life is now lost in this bewildering night at the thought of him who has the nature of wealth

kural.deTranslation: To lift from want he left me afar His thought makes my eyes blush the flower
kural.deExplanation: While we endure the unbearable sorrow, your eyes weep for him who is gone afar, and shun (the sight of) fragrant flowers

kural.deTranslation: My pale tearful eyes betray The hardness of my husband, away
kural.deExplanation: The discoloured eyes that shed tears profusely seem to betray the unkindness of our beloved

kural.deTranslation: These arms that swelled on nuptial day Now shrunk proclaim \"He is away\"
kural.deExplanation: The shoulders that swelled on the day of our union (now) seem to announce our separation clearly (to the public)

kural.deTranslation: Bracelets slip off the arms that have Lost old beauty for He took leave
kural.deExplanation: In the absence of your consort, your shoulders having lost their former beauty and fulness, your bracelets of pure gold have become loose

kural.deTranslation: Bereft of bracelets and old beauty Arms tell the cruel's cruelty
kural.deExplanation: The (loosened) bracelets, and the shoulders from which the old beauty has faded, relate the cruelty of the pitiless one

kural.deTranslation: Arms thin, armlets loose make you call My sire cruel; that pains my soul
kural.deExplanation: I am greatly pained to hear you call him a cruel man, just because your shoulders are reduced and your bracelets loosened

kural.deTranslation: Go and tell the cruel, O mind  Bruit ov'r my arms and glory find
kural.deExplanation: Can you O my soul! gain glory by relating to the (so-called) cruel one the clamour of my fading shoulders?

kural.deTranslation: The front of this fair one O paled As my clasping arms loosed their hold
kural.deExplanation: When I once loosened the arms that were in embrace, the forehead of the gold-braceleted women turned sallow

kural.deTranslation: Cool breeze crept between our embrace Her large rain-cloud-eyes paled at once
kural.deExplanation: When but a breath of breeze penetrated our embrace, her large cool eyes became sallow

kural.deTranslation: Pale eyes pained seeing the pallor Of the bright forehead of this fair
kural.deExplanation: Was it at the sight of what the bright forehead had done that the sallowness of her eyes became sad?

kural.deTranslation: Think of, O heart, some remedy To cure this chronic malady
kural.deExplanation: O my soul, will you not think and tell me some medicine be it what it may, that can cure this incurable malady?

kural.deTranslation: Bless O mind! you pine in vain For me he has no love serene
kural.deExplanation: Is folly, fare thee well my heart!

kural.deTranslation: O mind, why pine and sit moody? Who made you so pale lacks pity
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! why remain (here) and suffer thinking (of him)? There are no lewd thoughts (of you) in him who has caused you this disease of sorrow

kural.deTranslation: Take these eyes and meet him, O heart Or their hunger will eat me out
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! take my eyes also with you, (if not), these would eat me up (in their desire) to see him

kural.deTranslation: He spurns our love and yet, O mind, Can we desert him as unkind?
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! can he who loves not though he is beloved, be forsaken saying he hates me (now)?

kural.deTranslation: Wrath is false, O heart, face-to face Sans huff, you rush to his sweet embrace
