kural.deExplanation: O my soul! when you see the dear one who remove dislike by intercourse, you are displeased and continue to be so Nay, your displeasure is (simply) false

kural.deTranslation: Off with love O mind, or shame I cannot endure both of them
kural.deExplanation: O my good soul, give up either lust or honour, as for me I can endure neither

kural.deTranslation: Without pity he would depart! You sigh and seek his favour, poor heart!
kural.deExplanation: You are a fool, O my soul! to go after my departed one, while you mourn that he is not kind enough to favour you

kural.deTranslation: The lover lives in Self you know; Whom you think, mind to whom you go?
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! to whom would you repair, while the dear one is within yourself?

kural.deTranslation: Without a thought he deserted us To think of him will make us worse
kural.deExplanation: If I retain in my heart him who has left me without befriending me, I shall lose even the (inward) beauty that remains

kural.deTranslation: Passion's axe shall break the door Of reserve bolted with my honour
kural.deExplanation: The axe of lust can break the door of chastity which is bolted with the bolt of modesty

kural.deTranslation: The thing called lust is a heartless power It sways my mind at midnight hour
kural.deExplanation: Even at midnight is my mind worried by lust, and this one thing, alas! is without mercy

kural.deTranslation: How to hide this lust which shows Itself while I sneeze unawares!
kural.deExplanation: I would conceal my lust, but alas, it yields not to my will but breaks out like a sneeze

kural.deTranslation: I was proud of my sex-reserve Lo lust betrays what I preserve
kural.deExplanation: I say I would be firm, but alas, my malady breaks out from its concealment and appears in public

kural.deTranslation: Dignity seeks not a deserter But Love-sick is its innovator
kural.deExplanation: The dignity that would not go after an absent lover is not known to those who are sticken by love

kural.deTranslation: O Grief, my deserter you seek Of your caprice what shall I speak!
kural.deExplanation: The sorrow I have endured by desiring to go after my absent lover, in what way is it excellent?

kural.deTranslation: When lover's love does what it desires We forget all shame unawares
kural.deExplanation: I know nothing like shame when my beloved does from love (just) what is desired (by me)

kural.deTranslation: The cheater of many wily arts His tempting words break through women's hearts
kural.deExplanation: Are not the enticing words of my trick-abounding roguish lover the weapon that breaks away my feminine firmness?

kural.deTranslation: In huff I went and felt at ease Heat to heart in sweet embrace
kural.deExplanation: I said I would feign dislike and so went (away); (but) I embraced him the moment I say my mind began to unite with him!

kural.deTranslation: To feign dislike is it not rare  For mates who melt like fat in fire?
kural.deExplanation: Is it possible for those whose hearts melt like fat in the fire to say they can feign a strong dislike and remain so?

kural.deTranslation: My eyes are dim lustre-bereft Worn fingers count days since he left
kural.deExplanation: My finger has worn away by marking (on the wall) the days he has been absent while my eyes have lost their lustre and begin to fail

kural.deTranslation: Beauty pales and my bracelets slide; Why not forget him now, bright maid?
kural.deExplanation: O you bright-jewelled maid, if I forget (him) today, my shoulders will lose their beauty even in the other life and make my bracelets loose

kural.deTranslation: Will as guide he went to win Yet I live-to see him again
kural.deExplanation: I still live by longing for the arrival of him who has gone out of love for victory and with valour as his guide

kural.deTranslation: My heart in rapture heaves to see His retun with love to embrace me
kural.deExplanation: My heart is rid of its sorrow and swells with rapture to think of my absent lover returning with his love

kural.deTranslation: Let me but gaze and gaze my spouse sallow on my soft shoulders files
kural.deExplanation: May I look on my lover till I am satisfied and thereafter will vanish the sallowness of my slender shoulders

kural.deTranslation: Let my spouse return just a day Joy-drink shall drive my pain away
kural.deExplanation: May my husband return some day; and then will I enjoy (him) so as to destroy all this agonizing sorrow

kural.deTranslation: If my eye-like lord returneth Shall I sulk or clasp or do both?
kural.deExplanation: On the return of him who is as dear as my eyes, am I displeased or am I to embrace (him); or am I to do both?

kural.deTranslation: May the king fight and win and give And with my wife I will feast this eve!
kural.deExplanation: Let the king fight and gain (victories); (but) let me be united to my wife and feast the evening

kural.deTranslation: One day seems as seven to those Who yearn return of distant spouse
kural.deExplanation: To those who suffer waiting for the day of return of their distant lovers one day is as long as seven days

kural.deTranslation: When her heart is broken, what is The good of meeting and love-embrace?
kural.deExplanation: After (my wife) has died of a broken heart, what good will there be if she is to receive me, has received me, or has even embraced me?

kural.deTranslation: You hide; but your painted eyes Restraint off, report your surmise
kural.deExplanation: Though you would conceal (your feelings), your painted eyes would not, for, transgressing (their bounds), they tell (me) something

kural.deTranslation: With seemly grace and stem-like arms The simple she has ample charms
kural.deExplanation: Unusually great is the female simplicity of your maid whose beauty fills my eyes and whose shoulders resemble the bamboo

kural.deTranslation: Something shines through her jewelled charm Like thread shining through wreathed gem
kural.deExplanation: There is something that is implied in the beauty of this woman, like the thread that is visible in a garland of gems

kural.deTranslation: Like scent in bud secrets conceal In the bosom of her half smile
kural.deExplanation: There is something in the unmatured smile of this maid like the fragrance that is contained in an unblossomed bud

kural.deTranslation: The close-bangled belle's hidden thought Has a cure for my troubled heart She to Her Maid
kural.deExplanation: The well-meant departure of her whose bangles are tight-fitting contains a remedy that can cure my great sorrow

kural.deTranslation: His over-kind close embrace sooths; But makes me feel, loveless, he parts
kural.deExplanation: The embrace that fills me with comfort and gladness is capable of enduring (my former) sorrow and meditating on his want of love

kural.deTranslation: Quick, my bracelets read before The mind of my lord of cool shore
kural.deExplanation: My bracelets have understood before me the (mental) separation of him who rules the cool seashore

kural.deTranslation: My lover parted but yesterday; With sallowness it is seventh day The Maid Tells Him
kural.deExplanation: It was but yesterday my lover departed (from me); and it is seven days since my complexion turned sallow

kural.deTranslation: She views her armlets, her tender arms And then her feet; these are her norms
kural.deExplanation: She looked at her bracelets, her tender shoulders, and her feet; this was what she did there (significantly)

kural.deTranslation: To express love-pangs by eyes and pray Is womanhood's womanly way
kural.deExplanation: To express their love-sickness by their eyes and resort to begging bespeaks more than ordinary female excellence

kural.deTranslation: Rapture at thought and joy when seen Belong to love and not to wine
kural.deExplanation: To please by thought and cheer by sight is peculiar, not to liquor but lust

kural.deTranslation: When passion grows palmyra-tall Sulking is wrong though millet-small
kural.deExplanation: If women have a lust that exceeds even the measure of the palmyra fruit, they will not desire (to feign) dislike even as much as the millet

kural.deTranslation: Though slighting me he acts his will My restless eyes would see him still
kural.deExplanation: Though my eyes disregard me and do what is pleasing to my husband, still will they not be satisfied unless they see him

kural.deTranslation: Huff I would, maid, but I forget; And leap to embrace him direct
kural.deExplanation: My heart, forgetting all, could not its love restrain

kural.deTranslation: When close I see not lord's blemish Like eyes that see not painter's brush
kural.deExplanation: Like the eyes which see not the pencil that paints it, I cannot see my husband's fault (just) when I meet him

kural.deTranslation: When he's with me I see not fault And nought but fault when he is not
kural.deExplanation: When I see my husband, I do not see any faults; but when I do not see him, I do not see anything but faults

kural.deTranslation: To leap in stream which carries off When lord is close to feign a huff
kural.deExplanation: Like those who leap into a stream which they know will carry them off, why should a wife feign dislike which she knows cannot hold out long?

kural.deTranslation: Like wine to addicts that does disgrace Your breast, O thief, is for my embrace!
kural.deExplanation: O you rogue! your breast is to me what liquor is to those who rejoice in it, though it only gives them an unpleasant disgrace

kural.deTranslation: Flower-soft is love; a few alone Know its delicacy so fine
kural.deExplanation: Sexual delight is more delicate than a flower, and few are those who understand its real nature

kural.deTranslation: She feigned dislike awhile but flew Faster for embrace than I do
kural.deExplanation: She once feigned dislike in her eyes, but the warmth of her embrace exceeded my own

kural.deTranslation: You see, his heart is his alone; Why not my heart be all my own?
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! although you have seen how his soul stands by him, how is it you do not stand by me?

kural.deTranslation: O heart, you see how he slights me Yet you clasp him as if friendly
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! although you have known him who does not love me, still do you go to him, saying "he will not be displeased."

kural.deTranslation: You follow him at will Is it \"The fallen have no friends\" my heart?
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! do you follow him at pleasure under the belief that the ruined have no friends?

kural.deTranslation: You won't sulk first and then submit Who will then consult you, my heart?
kural.deExplanation: O my soul! you would not first seem sulky and then enjoy (him); who then would in future consult you about such things?

kural.deTranslation: Frets to gain and fears loss in gain O my heart suffers ceaseless pain
kural.deExplanation: My soul fears when it is without him; it also fears when it is with him; it is subject to incessant sorrow

kural.deTranslation: My itching mind eats me anon As I muse on him all alone
kural.deExplanation: My mind has been (here) in order to eat me up (as it were) whenever I think of him in my solitude

kural.deTranslation: I forget shame but not his thought In mean foolish mind I'm caught
kural.deExplanation: I have even forgotten my modesty, having been caught in my foolish mind which is not dignified enough to forget him

kural.deTranslation: My heart living in love of him Hails his glory ignoring blame
kural.deExplanation: My soul which clings to life thinks only of his (own) gain in the belief that it would be disgraceful for it to despise him

kural.deTranslation: Who support a man in grief If lover's heart denies relief?
kural.deExplanation: Who would help me out of one's distress, when one's own soul refuses help to one?

kural.deTranslation: Why wonder if strangers disown When one's own heart is not his own?
kural.deExplanation: It is hardly possible for strangers to behave like relations, when one's own soul acts like a stranger

kural.deTranslation: Feign sulk; embrace him not so that We can see his distress a bit
kural.deExplanation: Let us witness awhile his keen suffering; just feign dislike and embrace him not

kural.deTranslation: Sulking is the salt of love; but Too much of it spoils the taste Wife Addresses Husband
kural.deExplanation: A little dislike is like salt in proportion; to prolong it a little is like salt a little too much

kural.deTranslation: To leave the sulker unembraced Is to grieve the one sorely grieved
kural.deExplanation: For men not to embrace those who have feigned dislike is like torturing those already in agony

kural.deTranslation: To comfort not lady in pout Is to cut the fading plant at root He within Himself
kural.deExplanation: Not to reconcile those who have feigned dislike is like cutting a faded creeper at its root

kural.deTranslation: Pouting of flower-eyed has To pure good mates a lovely grace
kural.deExplanation: An increased shyness in those whose eyes are like flowers is beautiful even to good and virtuous husbands

kural.deTranslation: Love devoid of frowns and pets Misses its ripe and unripe fruits
kural.deExplanation: Sexual pleasure, without prolonged and short-lived dislike, is like too ripe, and unripe fruit

kural.deTranslation: \"Will union take place soon or late?\" In lover's pout this leaves a doubt
kural.deExplanation: The doubt as to whether intercourse would take place soon or not, creates a sorrow (even) in feigned dislike

kural.deTranslation: What's the good of grieving lament When concious lover is not present?
kural.deExplanation: What avails sorrow when I am without a wife who can understand the cause of my sorrow?

kural.deTranslation: Water delights in a shady grove And sulking in souls of psychic love
kural.deExplanation: Like water in the shade, dislike is delicious only in those who love

kural.deTranslation: My heart athirst would still unite With her who me in sulking left!
kural.deExplanation: It is nothing but strong desire that makes her mind unite with me who can leave her to her own dislike

kural.deTranslation: I shrink to clasp you bosom lewd To the gaze of all ladies exposed
kural.deExplanation: You are given to prostitution; all those who are born as womankind enjoy you with their eyes in an ordinary way I will not embrace you

kural.deTranslation: He sneezed while we went on sulking Expecting me to say \"live long\"
kural.deExplanation: When I continued to be sulky he sneezed and thought I would (then) wish him a long life

kural.deTranslation: \"For which lady?\" she widely cries While I adorn myself with flowers
kural.deExplanation: Even if I were adorned with a garland of branch-flowers, she would say I did so to show it to another woman

kural.deTranslation: \"I love you more than all\" I said \"Than whom, than whom?\" she sulked and chid
kural.deExplanation: When I said I loved her more than any other woman, she said "more than others, yes, more than others," and remained sulky

kural.deTranslation: \"In this life we won't part\" I told Her eyes at once with tears were filled
kural.deExplanation: When I said I would never part from her in this life her eyes were filled with tears

kural.deTranslation: I said I thought of you She left Her embrace crying \"Oft you forget\"
kural.deExplanation: When I said I had remembered her, she said I had forgotten her and relaxing her embrace, began to feign dislike

kural.deTranslation: I sneezed; she blessed; then changed and wept  \"You sneezed now at which lady's thought?\"
kural.deExplanation: When I sneezed she blessed me, but at once changed (her mind) and wept, asking, "At the thought of whom did you sneeze?"

kural.deTranslation: I repressed sneeze; she wept crying \"Your thoughts from me you are hiding\"
kural.deExplanation: When I suppressed my sneezing, she wept saying, "I suppose you (did so) to hide from me your own people's remembrance of you"

kural.deTranslation: I try to coax her and she remarks \"Your coaxing others thus this marks\"
kural.deExplanation: 'I see', quoth she, 'to other folks How you are wondrous kind' Even when I try to remove her dislike, she is displeased and says, "This is the way you behave

kural.deTranslation: I think and gaze at her; she chides: \"On whom your thought just now abides?\"
kural.deExplanation: Even when I look on her contemplating (her beauty), she is displeased and says, "With whose thought have you (thus) looked on my person?"

kural.deTranslation: He is flawless; but I do pout So that his loving ways show out
kural.deExplanation: Although my husband is free from defects, the way in which he embraces me is such as to make me feign dislike

kural.deTranslation: Fading first, love blooms and outlives The petty pricks that pouting gives
kural.deExplanation: His love will increase though it may (at first seem to) fade through the short-lived distress caused by (my) dislike

kural.deTranslation: Is there a heaven like sulk beneath Of hearts that join like water and earth?
kural.deExplanation: Is there a celestial land that can please like the feigned dislike of those whose union resembles that of earth and water?

kural.deTranslation: In long pout after embrace sweet A weapon is up to break my heart
kural.deExplanation: In prolonged dislike after an embrace there is a weapon that can break my heart

kural.deTranslation: Though free form faults, one feels the charms Of feigned release from lover's arms
kural.deExplanation: Though free from defects, men feel pleased when they cannot embrace the delicate shoulders of those whom they love

kural.deTranslation: Sweeter than meal is digestion And sulk in love than union
kural.deExplanation: To digest what has been eaten is more delightful than to eat more; likewise love is more delightful in dislike than intercourse

kural.deTranslation: The yielder wins in lover's pout Reunited joy brings it out
kural.deExplanation: Those are conquerors whose dislike has been defeated and that is proved by the love (which

kural.deTranslation: Shall not our pouting again give The dew-browed joy of joint love?
kural.deExplanation: Will I enjoy once more through her dislike, the pleasure of that love that makes her forehead perspire?

kural.deTranslation: Sulk on O belle of shining jewels! Prolong O night! our delight swells!
kural.deExplanation: May the bright-jewelled one feign dislike, and may the night be prolonged for me to implore her!

kural.deTranslation: Bouderie is lovers' delight Its delight grows when they unite
kural.deExplanation: Dislike adds delight to love; and a hearty embrace (thereafter) will add delight to dislike
